prompt: Which of the following describes all solutions to $-2x \ge 8$?
hint: Only one step is needed here, but look at the sign of the number you will divide by. It matters for an inequality.

hints.text: Only one step is needed here, but look at the sign of the number you will divide by. It matters for an inequality.
Divide both sides by $-2$ to isolate $x$. Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality, so $\ge$ becomes $\le$.
Since $8 \div (-2) = -4$ and the sign reverses, the solution is $x \le -4$, which is choice B.

learningObjective: Apply the sign-flip rule when dividing an inequality by a negative.
explanation: Divide both sides by $-2$ to isolate $x$. Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality, so the result is $x \le -4$.
Test a value in that set, such as $x = -5$: $-2(-5) = 10$, which is at least $8$, so it works.
Test a value outside the set, such as $x = 0$: $-2(0) = 0$, which is not at least $8$. The solution is $x \le -4$, choice B.

alternativeExplanations.title: Avoid the flip entirely
steps: Then subtract $8$: $-8 \ge 2x$, and divide by the *positive* $2$: $-4 \ge x$, which is $x \le -4$.
Keeping the variable coefficient positive means you never have to remember the flip rule at all.
